'''Christopher Edmond Hunter''' (born July 7, 1984)<ref name="Michigan player">{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050416051859/http://www.mgoblue.com/bio.cfm?bio_id=634&section_id=230&top=2&level=3|archivedate=April 16, 2005|title=2004-05 Michigan Men's Basketball: 31 Chris Hunter|publisher=University of Michigan|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/bio.cfm?bio_id=634&section_id=230&top=2&level=3|accessdate=April 3, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and currently works as the Director of Operations for the University of Michigan men's basketball team, where he also played [[college basketball]]. Before joining the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball]] staff, he played in several professional leagues. Most notably, he played in 60 games for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the NBA, was an [[NBA Development League]] All-star in 2009 and played abroad.

==Professional career==
[[File:Chris Hunter 4171540862 13be4ded2a o.jpg|left|thumb|Hunter as a [[Golden State Warrior]] in 2009]]
In 2006, Hunter signed with Herens Basket of Switzerland before being released before the start of the season. He then signed with [[AZS Koszalin]] of Poland.

In 2007, Hunter signed with [[Leuven Bears|Spotter Leuven]] of the [[BNXT League]]. He was later released in December 2007 due to injury.

In November 2008, Hunter was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]]. He was an NBA D League All-Star in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/chris-hunter/5233|title=Chris Hunter|accessdate=April 3, 2020|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=University of Michigan}}</ref> On April 14, 2009, Hunter signed with the [[New York Knicks]]. On October 22, he was waived by the Knicks before appearing in a regular season game.<ref name=realgm>[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Chris-Hunter/Summary/1595 Chris Hunter Player Profile – RealGM]</ref> On November 1, he was re-acquired by the Mad Ants. On November 20, Hunter signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]], making him the first call-up of the 2009–10 NBA D-League season.<ref name="realgm" />

Hunter joined the Knicks for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On October 30, 2010, he was re-acquired by the Mad Ants. On December 28, Hunter was waived by the Mad Ants due to an injury.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/12/28/former-gsw-call-up-chris-hunter-out-for-season-torn-achilles/ |title=Former Warriors Call-Up Chris Hunter Out for Season With Torn Achilles |access-date=2010-12-30 |archive-date=2011-02-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110202172131/http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/12/28/former-gsw-call-up-chris-hunter-out-for-season-torn-achilles |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In November 2011, Hunter was again re-acquired by the Mad Ants. On December 12, 2011, he signed with the Knicks. However, Hunter was waived by New York on December 22. He then subsequently returned to the Mad Ants. In January 2012, Hunter was again waived due to injury.<ref name="realgm" /> He later joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2012 NBA Summer League]].

On November 5, 2013, Hunter was re-acquired by the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/fortwayne/2013_draft.html |title=Mad Ants Chose 5 in NBA D-League Draft |access-date=2013-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204094611/http://www.nba.com/dleague/fortwayne/2013_draft.html |archive-date=2013-12-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 23, he was waived by the Mad Ants.

==Post-playing career==
On September 5, 2014, Hunter was named as the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]' Director of Player Personnel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/09/former_wolverine_chris_hunter.html|title=Former Wolverine Chris Hunter named Michigan basketball director of player personnel|date=5 September 2014}}</ref> On August 4, 2017, Michigan promoted Hunter from director of player personnel to director of basketball operations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2017/08/michigan_basketball_confirms_c_1.html|title=Michigan basketball announces coaching hires; Chris Hunter promoted|accessdate=August 8, 2017|date=August 5, 2017|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=McMann, Aaron}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/08/04/michigan-hires-yaklich-and-haynes-as-assistants/104304628/|title=Michigan hires Yaklich and Haynes as assistants|accessdate=August 8, 2017|date=August 4, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
